newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR says Western force still needed in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR says Western force still needed in Zaire.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency urged Western powers on Tuesday not to drop plans for the deployment of a Western military force in east Zaire, saying it was needed urgently in Bukavu area to reach 500,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees.

"There's a big job for a multi-national force to be done in east Zaire. Its priority should now be Bukavu where there are still half a million refugees. We need help. This is a huge job," UNHCR spokeswoman Christiane Berthiaume told a news briefing.

Bethiaume said UNHCR had been denied access to Bukavu area by Tutsi rebels who control the area and that the multi-national force was needed urgently to open the border, provide access to the region and the refugees.

Many countries have urged a re-think on plans for the multinational task force after 500,000 Rwandan Hutus returned home from Goam region further north following Tutsi rebel shelling of Mugunga camp which forced Hutu militia to flee.

The United States, Britain and South Africa were reluctant volunteers in the first place and have seized on the mass migration as a sign that the force should be radically sized down or even scrapped.

The Washington Post reported in Tuesday's edition that senior U.S. officials had tentatively concluded that the force is no longer needed and Canada's defence minister, Don Young, seemed to be edging towards the same view.
